text: I’ll model the half-domain on the exposed side of the mounting wall: streamwise \(x\), span \(y=0\) to \(0.20\) m, and airfoil thickness in \(z\). The root leading edge is at \(x=0\); the domain will run from \(-0.48\) to \(1.08\) m, from the root wall to \(y=0.56\) m, and \(z=\pm0.36\) m. I’ll loft sampled NACA 2412 root/tip sections, subtract the wing from the box, export conformal patch STLs, and use snappyHexMesh after a coarse geometry inspection. First I’m checking the installed algebra-mode loft interfaces so the authored script is reproducible.
That helper name is not present in the installed build123d, so I’ll locate the installed wire/loft constructors before creating geometry.
The API lists `Polyline(..., close=True)` and `loft(sections=...)`; I’ll confirm their exact runtime signatures and then construct the first solid.

I’ll now create the coarsest CAD version in metres. The NACA sections use cosine-spaced points and the closed-trailing-edge coefficient; the tip is a pure chord scaling, so there is no sweep or twist. I’ll subtract the loft from the wall-bounded box, print the requested dimensions, and render the resulting fluid volume and wing.

The preview shows the intended unswept tapered wing attached to the \(y=0\) wall inside the box. The boolean has 127 faces, consistent with six domain faces plus 120 ruled wing skin strips and one exposed tip cap. I’ll inspect face geometry and plane normals to label patches by their authored planes—not by bounding-box position.

The inspection confirms seven planar faces: the six authored domain planes and the exposed wing tip; all 120 loft skin strips are B-splines. The \(y=0\) root-wall face has the airfoil footprint removed, while the small \(y=0.2\) face is the wing tip. I’ll now export all five named patches in one conformal tessellation call.

The conformal export is closed and consistently wound: 536 triangles with zero open, flipped, or non-manifold edges. For the coarse mesh I’ll use a roughly 40 mm background grid and snappy refinement to about 5 mm at the wing. The box boundaries will be named directly in `blockMesh`; snappy will cut the open-at-root wing skin into the wall-bounded fluid mesh. No boundary layers yet—the first goal is a valid coarse external mesh.
The coarse meshing dictionaries are ready. I’ll generate the background mesh, extract the wing’s leading/trailing and tip features, then run snappyHexMesh in place.

snappyHexMesh requires the case-level numerical dictionaries even though no solver will be run. I’ll add minimal valid `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` files, then rerun the mesh generation so the accepted build script contains the complete successful sequence.
The support dictionaries are now present. I’ll regenerate all mesh stages and report snappy’s final cell count and patch creation.

The coarse snappy mesh completed with 28,978 cells and no internal quality-control errors. I’ll run the binding `checkMesh` and inspect the boundary table to verify all five requested mesh patches are present.

`checkMesh` passes: one connected region, five patches, maximum non-orthogonality \(44.2^\circ\), maximum skewness 1.61, and 28,978 cells. I’ll now render the actual mesh near the wing (not just the CAD) to confirm the taper, root attachment, and local refinement visually.

The OpenFOAM mesh has been converted to VTK successfully. I’ll make a two-panel inspection: a 3D close-up of the meshed wing and a mid-span \(y=0.10\) m slice showing the local cell refinement around the airfoil.

The 3D panel confirms local refinement and the tapered planform, but the slice panel was viewed edge-on. I’ll correct the camera to look normal to the spanwise slice so the NACA cross-section and surrounding cells are visible.

The corrected mid-span view shows the expected cambered NACA section, a clean body-fitted cut, and approximately 5 mm near-surface cells. Before finishing, I’ll numerically verify the NACA 2412 defining ratios and the requested domain offsets from the same equations and CAD parameters used to build the shape.

The mesh and geometry checks are complete. The only intentional zero-thickness feature is the mathematically closed NACA trailing edge, so I am recording that in advance for the minimum-wall-thickness advisory; it is not a missing surface or mesh gap.

The completion gate found that the STL manifest does not record the same fluid-side point used by snappyHexMesh. I’ll fix the manifest rather than waive it by re-exporting the conformal patches with the validated outside-wing point \((-0.20,\,0.10,\,0.10)\) m.
The exporter supports explicit `location_in_mesh`; I’ll re-export the same five patch sets with that point so the manifest and snappy dictionary agree. No geometry or mesh coordinates change.
The manifest now records the exact fluid-side point used for meshing. I’ll run the completion gates again, retaining only the intentional sharp-trailing-edge thickness waiver.
